### LoginMethodKind

```ts
type LoginMethodKind = "api_key" | "subscription";
```

How a person proves they may use a provider: an API key or their subscription
sign-in.

```ts
}>;
```

One sign-in method a provider offers, labelled by its owner.

```ts
type LoginProvider = Readonly<{
  id: string;

}>;
```

One model provider in the registry. Names come from data, never code.

```ts
type LoginHost = "local" | "hosted";
```

---

```ts

```

### ReloadSource

```ts
type ReloadSource = Readonly<object &
  | {
  effect: "now";
  reload: (signal) => Promise<void>;
}
  | {
  effect: "next_turn";
}
  | {
  effect: "unsupported";
  reason: string;
}>;
```

One category a host can account for in `/reload`, described by the owner that
already holds it. Nothing here caches, restarts or replaces anything: `now`
re-reads through the owner's own refresh, `next_turn` names a source the owner
already re-reads at the start of every turn, and `unsupported` names a category
with no safe re-read or replace lifecycle today.

---

```ts
  sourceId: string;
  namespace: string;
  sources: () => readonly ReloadSource[];
}>;
```

Where one `/reload` contribution comes from and what it can report.

### runSlashDraft()

```ts
function runSlashDraft(
  draft,
  commands,
  send,
  origin,
): Promise<WhistleExecutionOutcome | undefined>;
```

Run one composer draft: a prompt goes to `send`, a `/command` runs through
Whistle. A grammar that asks for a request id keeps the same id across retries
of the same draft until the command is handled.

| Parameter  | Type                            |
| ---------- | ------------------------------- |
| `draft`    | `string`                        |
| `commands` | [`SlashRuntime`](#slashruntime) |
| `send`     | () => `void`                    |
| `origin`   | `WhistleExecutionOrigin`        |

#### Returns

`Promise`\<`WhistleExecutionOutcome` \| `undefined`\>
